newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: PRESS DIGEST - S.Korean newspapers - March 20.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - S.Korean newspapers - March 20.

text.p: The following is a summary of major stories in leading South Korean newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Seoul. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not guarantee their accuracy. Telephone: (822) 727-5650. Fax: (822) 727-5666.
- Sammi Steel Co. becomes insolvent: other Sammi Group affiliates likely to go bankrupt successively.
- North Korean leader Kim Jong-il fears that worsening food problems could set off rioting in his tightly controlled country, a South Korean newspaper reported yesterday.
- U.S.govenment expected to unfreeze North Korean bank accounts, according to a North Korean report.
- Park Kyung-sik was summoned and questioned overnight in connection to a scandal involving the president's second son Kim hyun-chul.
- Hyundai Eelectronics broke ground for the a new semiconductor factory in Scotland.
- Sammi Steel became insolvent on Wednesday after applying for court receivership.
- The central Bank of Korea is expected to give emergency funds to Korea First Bank which is the main creditor to insolvent Sammi Steel.
